name: new_ornament
title: Helper to define the contents of a pillar

origin.description: This function is useful if your data renders differently depending on the available width. In this case, implement the pillar_shaft() method for your class to return a subclass of "pillar_shaft" and have the format() method for this subclass call new_ornament(). See the implementation of pillar_shaft.numeric() and format.pillar_shaft_decimal() for an example.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A character vector with formatting, can use ANSI styles e.g. provided by the cli package.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: An optional width of the resulting pillar, computed from x if missing.

translation.description: This function is useful if your data renders differently depending on the available width. In this case, implement the pillar_shaft() method for your class to return a subclass of "pillar_shaft" and have the format() method for this subclass call new_ornament(). See the implementation of pillar_shaft.numeric() and format.pillar_shaft_decimal() for an example.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A character vector with formatting. ANSI sequences may be included; they do not count toward the width.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: An optional width of the resulting pillar, computed from x if missing.

arguments.name: align
arguments.text: Alignment, one of "left" or "right". None stays unset and formats as left.

translation.details: The ornament stores the character vector, the alignment, and the width. format() pads with align(). print() writes a <pillar_ornament> header and then the formatted lines. When pillar.bold is true, that header is passed through the bold style. When it is false, the header is plain. The data lines are not colored.
translation.value: A pillar ornament. Printing it shows the header and the aligned lines.
